In-process for scrip 503681: plain httpx index 403, _api_json index 118 rows (June 2026), and the XBRL is 200 over plain httpx and parses. Only the index call is blocked. batch-3 VERDICTS.md noted this 403 as an honest-degrade observation but it was never registered. verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:252-265: list_workspaces GETs '/workspaces' (line 255) and get_workspace GETs '/workspaces/{id}' (line 263), but sidecar/routers/workspace.py:21 is APIRouter(prefix='/workspace'). list_workspaces also skips the module's _get_list bare-list wrap (mcp_server.py:113), and GET /workspace returns a bare list[str].
verdicts.fix_shape: In mcp_server.py, list_workspaces becomes 'return await _get_list("/workspace", "workspaces")'. get_workspace GETs f'/workspace/{quote(workspace_id, safe="")}' and maps an httpx.HTTPError to {'ok': False, 'error': ...} the way _get_list does, instead of a bare raise_for_status. Correct both docstrings. No REST contract change. A prefix-only fix is NOT enough: simulated, list_workspaces then fails with 'structured_content must be a dict or None. Got list'.
verdicts.acceptance_test: sidecar/tests/test_mcp_server.py: new test_workspace_tools_reach_the_workspace_router. With the bound-app client fixture and a scratch VYSTED_DATA_DIR, POST /workspace {'name':'t-ws','workspace':{'version':1}}. Assert call_tool('list_workspaces',{}) structured_content is a dict and 't-ws' in ['workspaces']; call_tool('get_workspace',{'workspace_id':'t-ws'}) == {'version':1}; get_workspace('missing') -> ok False with '404' in error. Add ('list_workspaces','/workspace') to test_list_tool_reports_a_failing_route_as_not_ok. Live: own sidecar, save a workspace, then a FastMCP in-memory Client over mcp_server._build_server() with VYSTED_SIDECAR_INTERNAL_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>: both tools is_error=False.
verdicts.note: Reproduced on own :52365: GET /workspaces and /workspaces/refaudit2-ws -> 404; /workspace and /workspace/refaudit2-ws -> 200. The real MCP tools, called through a FastMCP in-memory Client, both return is_error=True with 'Client error 404 Not Found for url …/workspaces'. With the path alone corrected (simulated by a rewriting transport), get_workspace works but list_workspaces still errors on the bare list. Tests only assert the tool names are registered and never call either tool. Severity kept high per the verifier: two v1.0 external MCP tools are dead for every client. The failure is loud and narrow, so this is the candidate for a medium downgrade if the collator grades it that way.

verdicts.root_cause: sidecar/services/symbol_resolver.py:1574: yf.Search(query, max_results=5, news_count=0) passes no timeout, so it inherits yfinance 1.3.0's timeout=30. The fix_shape's second clause ('pass an explicit yf.Search timeout') was dropped in batch-3 PLAN.md and never implemented.
verdicts.fix_shape: Pass an explicit short timeout at symbol_resolver.py:1574, e.g. timeout=_LIVE_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS with a ~5 s module constant (live misses measure 0.4-2.2 s). The existing except already records the failure and arms the 60 s _LIVE_FAILURE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS, so a hung Yahoo costs one short call instead of 30 s per concurrent miss. Update the 'up to 30 s' comment at agent_tools/resolve_symbol.py:52-53.
verdicts.acceptance_test: sidecar/tests/test_resolve_symbol_tool.py (or test_symbol_resolver.py): new test_live_lookup_passes_an_explicit_short_search_timeout. Monkeypatch yfinance.Search with a kwargs-recording class (quotes=[]); clear _live_cache and _live_cooldown_until; call symbol_resolver._live_lookup('zzqx nonexistent co','IN'); assert 'timeout' in kwargs and kwargs['timeout'] <= 10. Live: the scratch a010.py hang race (local never-answering HTTPS_PROXY) finishes in <= timeout+1 s instead of 31.07 s with max_gap_ms < 50, and a010-sat.py's unrelated to_thread waits <= timeout+2 s instead of 36.89 s.
verdicts.failure_sources: rc1-gate-round-2 (this audit, partial); batch-3 certified it; not in round-1 REFUTATION_AUDIT.json
verdicts.note: The loop-stall half holds. The regression tests pass, and in-process races on fresh phrasings show max loop gap 21 ms. Two llama3.1:8b agent runs on own :52365 (under the lock, fresh phrasings, resolve_symbol tool_use/tool_result read from the SSE transcript) kept /health under 92 ms. The verifier's grep holds: no timeout at symbol_resolver.py:1574, and the yfinance 1.3.0 signature defaults timeout=30. Measured cost at the candidate with a hung upstream: a single resolve_symbol call took 31.07 s. 12 concurrent misses (the default-executor size) blocked an unrelated asyncio.to_thread for 36.89 s, and that executor is shared by every to_thread in the sidecar. Residual rated medium, down from the entry's high, because the event loop itself is no longer stalled.
